metadata.title: Revisiting gender differences in personality: New evidence on big five domains and facets with large-scale samples from 27 nations

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PIAAC 2023 (PIAAC 2nd cycle; fielded 2022–23) public-use files for 27 participating countries, drawing probability samples of the adult population in each country (typically 4,000–5,000 respondents per country; total N=143,313 across the 27 countries). The manuscript describes the sampling as probability-based and emphasizes cross-country comparability of instruments, but it does not report the specific PIAAC weight variable(s) used in the analyses. Because the outcomes are country-comparable Big Five domain/facet scores and gender differences summarized across countries, analysts should apply the appropriate PIAAC sampling weights when estimating population-representative effects within each country and when aggregating across countries. The paper also harmonizes measurement across two Big Five inventory forms (BFI-2-S vs BFI-2-XS) by using the best available indicator per country (BFI-2-S where available; otherwise BFI-2-XS), with results reported as highly similar when using BFI-2-XS across all countries.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study does not model cognitive achievement outcomes with PIAAC Plausible Values; instead, it analyzes self-reported Big Five personality domain and facet scores that are provided as standardized scale scores in the public-use files. Because the dependent variables are not PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not describe a missing-data strategy (e.g., complete-case vs imputation), so missing-data handling is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses use PIAAC 2023 public-use files for 27 countries with available Big Five data. The paper states that 31 countries participated in PIAAC 2023, and 29 in the optional Big Five assessment, but only 27 countries were available as public-use files for the present analyses. For personality measurement, the study uses the best available Big Five indicator per country: BFI-2-S scores where available (16 countries) and BFI-2-XS scores otherwise (11 countries), and it reports that using BFI-2-XS for all countries yields highly similar findings. Facet-level analyses are restricted to the subset of 11 countries that fielded the BFI-2-S form (as indicated by the facet-level results and the subset size in the results section). The manuscript does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds) or an explicit missing-data rule in the provided text.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIAAC 2023 the study leveraged Gender (male/female), Country GDP per capita, Human Development Index (HDI) to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that The study uses PIAAC 2023 (PIAAC 2nd cycle; fielded 2022–23) public-use data from 27 countries (total N=143,313) to quantify gender differences in self-reported Big Five personality domains and facets using population-representative adult samples. It reports multivariate gender differences aggregated across countries using Mahalanobis distance (MD), finding an overall effect of MD=0.67, with women scoring higher than men most notably on Neuroticism (d=0.40) and Agreeableness (d=0.35), and smaller advantages on Conscientiousness (d=0.19) and Openness (d=0.11), while Extraversion shows no substantial domain-level difference. Cross-country variation is substantial (MD SD=0.09), with smaller differences in Singapore (MD=0.41) and larger differences in Germany, Norway, and Estonia (MD≈0.80). Associations with country-level indicators show that only Hofstede’s individualism-collectivism index is significantly related to the aggregated multivariate gender difference (17% explained variance; MD r=0.41), and facet-level patterns (subset of 11 countries) further highlight which facets drive domain effects. The paper does not report any ML model training or PV/missing-data handling strategy, and the country-level correlations are based on only 27 countries, limiting precision and sensitivity to outliers. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ML because the manuscript is not an empirical machine-learning prediction/classification study; it is a cross-national descriptive/associational analysis of gender differences in personality traits using PIAAC 2023. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no predictive targets, and no PV-based achievement modeling, which explains the empty main_findings and ml_techniques fields. The paper also does not provide a missing-data handling protocol in the provided text, so missing-data handling cannot be reconstructed from the excerpt.
